newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Olympics-Sydney organisers ask for time change.
newsitem.headline: Olympics-Sydney organisers ask for time change.

text.p: The organisers of the Sydney 2000 Olympics want to put clocks forward during the Games to provide an extra hour of daylight for competition late in the day.
The Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games (SOCOG) said the change would allow more sports to be played in the late afternoon, a popular time for athletes.
"We have come to the conclusion that it is necessary for the sporting success of the Games," SOCOG sports commission chairman John Coates told a news conference on Wednesday.
By making the annual change to summer time two months earlier than usual, SOCOG would be given greater flexibility in scheduling sports, particular in the event of bad weather, Coates said.

"It gives us more leeway when we might have wind or rain and some disruption," Coates said. SOCOG will lobby the governments of New South Wales and Queensland states to agree to the one-off change, but expects opposition from rural areas.
The 2000 Games will be held between September 15 and October 1, during the southern hemisphere spring, avoiding the sweltering summer heat in Australia.
As it stands, the sun sets at about six p.m. in September but if SOCOG's idea is accepted non-floodlit outdoor events could be staged until just before seven p.m.
Instead of clocks going forward one hour during the last weekend in October, as normal, the switch would occur on August 27, the week before the Olympic village opens, Coates said.
